title: "anytime() gives a different time depending on the machine"
ref: DAT-02
categories: [Dates]

::: {.piege .piege-statique}
```r
library(anytime)
anytime("2022-11-01", tz = "Europe/Paris")
```

```text
# workstation set to Europe/Paris
[1] "2022-11-01 CET"

# server or container set to UTC
[1] "2022-11-01 01:00:00 CET"
```
:::

This pitfall depends on the machine's time zone, so it cannot be replayed in the browser.

## Why

`anytime()` reads the text as a local time, in the system time zone (the `TZ` variable or the OS setting). The `tz` argument only comes into play afterwards, for display. On a workstation set to Paris, the string is read as midnight in Paris. On a Linux server or a Docker container, almost always set to UTC, it is read as midnight UTC, that is 1 a.m. in Paris.

The same script therefore gives different times locally and in production, with no error or warning. The gap looks like a Windows versus Linux difference, but what matters is the system time zone.

## The remedy

State the time zone at read time, with a function that uses it to interpret the text.

::: {.piege}
```{r}
as.POSIXct("2022-11-01", tz = "Europe/Paris")
```
:::
